points.why: It names the vacancies → overtime → burnout → vacancies reinforcing loop but never frames mandatory overtime as a quick fix that backfires (Fixes That Fail).
It roughly identifies the links each option touches, including (c) changing the incentive to push overtime, but never places them on leverage bands as parameter, rule and goal.
It flags that who sets the metric determines how hard (c) is, but it treats (c) as subsidiary rather than most powerful and never mentions testing options in a model.
It chooses the cap first, says the cap only manages the symptom while the hiring pipeline addresses the root cause, and notes that answer times will worsen during the transition.

pitfalls.why: It keeps the bonus as a later or conditional option and does not dismiss it on principle.

notes: It overstates that the cap is the only proposal that breaks the loop and calls (c) cheap and budget-independent, even though (c) changes the goal that drives the loop.
